blogs.title: When Sepsis Masks a TMA: Recognizing the Clinical Pivot
blogs.description: This post explores the diagnostic challenge of identifying Thrombotic Microangiopathy (TMA) when it is obscured by the 'noise' of overwhelming sepsis and Disseminated Intravascular Coagulation (DIC). We discuss the clinical transition point—where the primary infection stabilizes but hematological parameters continue to deteriorate—and how to pivot the diagnostic workup toward complement-mediated Hemolytic Uremic Syndrome (CM-HUS).

blogs.title: Beyond the Bite: Capnocytophaga canimorsus as a Fulminant Systemic Trigger
blogs.description: While often considered a minor zoonotic risk, Capnocytophaga canimorsus can lead to rapid, life-threatening sepsis and multi-organ failure. This post reviews the clinical presentation of C. canimorsus bacteraemia, the challenges of its fastidious growth in cultures, and its emerging role as a specific trigger for complement dysregulation in immunocompetent adults.

blogs.title: Navigating the TMA Maze: TTP, STEC-HUS, and the Diagnosis of Exclusion
blogs.description: Distinguishing between the various types of TMA is a critical bedside priority. This post provides a framework for differentiating Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) using ADAMTS13 activity, ruling out Shiga toxin-producing E. coli (STEC-HUS) via PCR, and ultimately arriving at a diagnosis of CM-HUS when standard complement levels (C3/C4) remain deceptively normal.

blogs.title: The Double-Edged Sword: Complement Activation as Defense and Destroyer
blogs.description: A deep dive into the pathophysiology of CM-HUS. We discuss the 'clinical paradox' where the host's essential complement system, required to clear encapsulated bacteria like C. canimorsus, can simultaneously trigger catastrophic endothelial damage. This post covers the concept of 'second hit' triggers in genetically predisposed individuals versus infection-triggered TMA in the general population.

blogs.title: The Therapeutic Tug-of-War: Timing Eculizumab in the Setting of Infection
blogs.description: This post addresses the high-stakes clinical dilemma of initiating terminal complement blockade (Eculizumab) in a patient with a history of bacteraemia. We discuss the risks of increased susceptibility to encapsulated organisms, the role of Plasma Exchange as a bridge, and the strategies for safe transition to complement inhibition, including vaccination and antimicrobial prophylaxis.
